# R446 — read-only forward test of the Strata upstream-sync skill

Date: 2026-10-14 (Asia/Tokyo)
Mode: read-only planning exercise. No fetch/network mutation, Git mutation, source edit, build, test, AST, GPU, process, environment, private JSON, or raw-log inspection. Only this report was written.

## Request evaluated

“子ブランチにスキルと検証レポートがある。主ブランチfeature/syclに反映し、区切りで自分のfork mainも更新、終わった枝を削除してほしい。XeStrata由来の別実験treeに高速化候補もあるが、同条件で主実装とは比較していない。今回はread-onlyの計画のみ。”

## Result

The current project skill yields a staged plan, and its read-only rule explicitly prevents carrying out the requested writes or measurements in this turn. For an eventual implementation, the safe target is a new integration worktree based on the then-current feature/sycl, with explicitly selected skill/report files. Do not merge K or Z wholesale: K is on the Xe experiment lineage, not descended from feature/sycl, and its full tree differs by thousands of files. Preserve original report/source commit provenance separately from product-tree adoption. Do not enable or merge the Xe-derived speed candidate: its evidence is local to Z and does not compare it against the actual feature/sycl implementation under a matched recipe.

No branch, PR, file, report, or deletion is ready to be changed on the evidence in this read-only request. Specific blockers and acceptance gates follow.

## Current source and Git facts

- The instructed project skill is /home/yayoi/orca/workspaces/Strata/sycl/.agents/skills/strata-upstream-sync/SKILL.md. It sets Niko1221/Strata as sole upstream, the user's PC as the optimization target, excludes CUDA/HIP work and XeStrata parity, names feature/sycl as the primary branch, requires child branches from its current commit, and says read-only requests end at investigation/planning (skill lines 14-33).
- The active user worktree is on feature/sycl at 4fa478f50f8da396e651e3ae862f8b1849d49b54. At inspection it had modified AGENTS.md and untracked .agents/ and .claude/ content. Preserve and review those existing edits; do not reset, overwrite, or make an integration commit in that worktree.
- Fork main is beddab2fd6b61631d73b39b7484bc9a585ebe1de and its ghq root was clean at inspection. feature/sycl and main diverge from d988955e141190bc079b58ab3d3038da637ad070: main has 285 commits not in feature/sycl, and feature has 143 not in main. This is not a routine fast-forward/promotion. Before a PR, reconcile the actual main tree into the primary branch without silently losing the SYCL changes or reverting main's upstream updates. The project skill names feature/sycl as source of truth; the specific merge/conflict resolution strategy remains open until those source diffs are reviewed.
- K, feat/strata-upstream-sync-skill-20261013 at 97f8b40ca99ec298c24d7ecc7b270e530d43194d, descends from 8b48d17c, whose parent is the Xe experiment line at 6035c4f9. It is not a child of feature/sycl; the merge base is 99f3dbd0b21d1401b3769e0c0d963913607f380b. Its committed skill is under .claude/skills/strata-upstream-sync, while the active feature worktree has a newer project skill under .agents/skills. K's committed reports include 2026-10-13-project-scope-skill-correction/REPORT.md and 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-skill-and-regression-audit/REPORT.md.
- Z, feat/layer-major-bulk-upload-20261013 at 28a7b9ae7ca5eba28eecd65f6453a7479c04fce8, is a XeStrata-derived experiment tree. The skill is explicit that Xe is a reference only. Its measured branch is not the feature/sycl product source.
- Commit 97f8b40 is also named by diag-decode-service-budget-20261014 and diag/bounded-decode-route-ledger-20261013; separate worktrees exist for those refs and feat/strata-upstream-sync-skill. Therefore “delete the finished skill branch” does not authorize deleting all aliases or the other diagnostic worktrees.
- The fork clone remote is origin at yqYo1/Strata. Niko is present in a separate clone, not as an origin remote on the fork clone. At a later authorized sync, verify the actual Niko tag/commit and remote direction before fetch; the retained v0.1.43 pin 7695859 is evidence for that snapshot, not proof that it is still the newest release.

## What the named reports and candidate establish

- K's project-scope-skill-correction report records earlier project-skill validation on K. It is not a validation receipt for files subsequently placed in feature/sycl. Re-run relevant source/document/skill checks in the destination worktree after copying; keep the historical receipt and add a new destination result instead of changing the old status.
- K's older upstream-sync-skill-and-regression-audit report includes historical wording about personal Codex installation and importing every non-inference feature. The current feature skill is project-local and makes Niko the only upstream. Keep that report as dated evidence, but add a correction/cross-reference so the old wording is not treated as current policy.
- Z's 2026-10-13-layer-major-bulk-upload README reports implementation qualification in the Xe tree and explicitly limits it: not full 256K, RESTORE, whole-model, or speed proof at that stage.
- Z's 2026-10-14-layer-bulk-stock-repeat README uses the unchanged upstream bench client and reports three samples: bulk prefill median 693.5 tok/s versus repeat-control 666.5; decode 8.1 versus 8.5. It says adoption is held, because decode regressed in the repeat control too and a bulk-specific decode regression is not established. This is a same-Z-tree comparison, not a matched comparison against feature/sycl. Preserve it as an experiment result and hypothesis, not as an accepted feature or a feature/sycl speed estimate.
- These markdown summaries are the reviewed evidence. Do not copy the entire K/Z bench/results trees to satisfy “bring the report”; select named compact reports and keep any necessary source/result provenance by commit/path. Do not promote or delete bulky evidence without checking current consumers under the artifact-retention policy.

## Action plan after a separate implementation request

1. **Freeze the inputs.** Check the current Niko target tag/SHA, fork origin/default, feature/main heads, exact child refs, worktree paths and dirty states. Read current AGENTS/artifact-retention policy and the reports/skill files named by commit and repository-relative path. Keep pristine upstream and existing dirty worktrees untouched. Create a fresh integration worktree from the current feature/sycl commit; do not create a child from K or Z.
2. **Define the exact artifact set.** Confirm which child carries the intended skill and which compact reports are to land on feature/sycl. Transfer only the project skill, supporting references/metadata, and requested reports or a concise superseding report. Update repository-relative links and distinguish historical test results from destination validation. Do not copy Xe product instructions, CUDA/HIP obligations, all historical benchmark files, or raw logs as a side effect.
3. **Preserve provenance while selecting the tree deliberately.** Keep original commit IDs recoverable as required by the skill, but do not use a history-only merge as proof of implementation. If a preservation merge is used, make its intended tree explicit and verify it still represents feature/sycl plus only reviewed artifact changes. Verify the actual feature tree contains the project skill at the supported project path, no global-install reference, and report/source links resolve.
4. **Inventory function and inference work separately.** For skill/report integration, validate project-local discovery, references, and report status/path only. Do not start an upstream feature migration absent from the request. Treat each Niko server/CLI/settings delta as applicable, equivalent, excluded with reason, pending, or adopted; CUDA/HIP inference remains outside scope. Treat the Xe bulk candidate only as a proposed component. If it is pursued later, port/adapt it on a fresh feature-based child and compare candidate-off/on on the intended PC with the same local engine/build, model and model hash, request/input, client revision, context/KV/chunk/cache/CPU/MTP settings, and output budget. Use at least three individual alternating samples per arm, record actual prompt/output counts and all failures, then extend repetitions if variance overlaps. For changed arithmetic/state, compare fixed-history logits/distribution/state and relevant RESTORE behavior; a Xe-vs-feature whole-engine rate alone cannot qualify adoption.
5. **Run checks only after implementation authorization.** First run skill/document checks and relevant host tests for files touched. Run API/CLI/setup tests for corresponding feature imports. Only after source review and safe small checks should the Main-owned GPU/model comparison be scheduled serially; isolate tracing/validation from performance runs. Keep the original result status, source/build/environment/input identities, per-sample results and next decision in compact committed reports.
6. **Reconcile feature and fork main before promotion.** Because the refs have diverged substantially, compare full trees and resolve whether/how current main is merged into feature/sycl before producing a PR. Preserve both branches' user functionality and the feature branch's validated SYCL paths; do not use ancestry alone or “ours” to hide missing source. Once the resulting feature branch has reviewed source and passing scoped checks, update fork main via a PR as the project skill requires; never commit directly to the ghq main root. After the PR is merged, pull the fork default into its clean root mirror and verify exact heads/tree.
7. **Retire only individually closed refs.** For each named branch, confirm the PR/integration is complete, commit SHA and needed reports remain reachable from a protected branch, no open PR/active worktree/untracked fixture/diagnostic consumer remains, and any necessary large fixture has a named retained consumer. Keep the preservation/deletion manifest with original refs, commit IDs, path/hash/reason. Remove its worktree before deleting that local branch; delete the remote branch only when the same evidence holds. The K shared SHA and Z's unmatched candidate are not currently safe retirement targets. Do not force-remove dirty worktrees.

## Confirmation gates and unresolved choices

Before executing the plan, confirm:
- The exact child refs and report paths intended for feature/sycl. K contains the skill and two skill reports; Z contains the bulk candidate and its two benchmark summaries. The request does not say which reports to transfer.
- Whether “update my fork main at milestones” means merge each scoped feature PR after its checks. The skill and git-workflow both imply a PR to yqYo1/Strata main, not direct edits to the default root.
- How to reconcile main's 285 unique commits with feature/sycl's 143 unique commits. This is a substantial source integration, not a branch deletion task; the choice must preserve current main behavior and feature inference paths.
- Which branch refs are considered finished. K's commit is shared by diagnostic aliases and worktrees; Z's speed candidate is explicitly unqualified against feature/sycl and should remain available.
- The exact PC, supported OS, model/build/runtime, and acceptable quality thresholds for a future same-condition candidate A/B. The current prompt supplies none of these details; no performance acceptance can be inferred.
- Whether a destination report should include only compact summaries or also structured individual measurements. The current instruction forbids inspection of private JSON/raw logs, so this plan does not assert their exact contents.

## Evidence read and limits

Read the current feature project skill and its integration/evaluation references, git-workflow skill, relevant committed K/Z markdown reports, branch/worktree refs, commit ancestry/counts, and read-only statuses. The provided registry v200 was not inspected, and private JSON/raw benchmark logs were not opened. No implementation, merge, test, measurement, PR, branch cleanup or file transfer was performed.
role: read-only proposal; Main decisions are in decisions.json
